1.sofaString: 103	Pt, *******, is a 3 week old male who is diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who is being  referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother and review of the medical records.   SW spent 45 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *******, resides with his parents in *****, *******.  They reside in ** ********* at ***** ** 39th Ave, *****, ** *****.  They live in * **** with city water and window a/c.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have some indoor cats and one outdoor cat.  The ********* is not kept in a shared area with the baby.  There is no smoking in the home.     Demographics:  Mother: ****** ******  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  31  Education:  Has earned 2 AA degrees in emergency medical services  Employment:  ******* Medical Transport (currently on leave)  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ****** *******  DOB:  **/**/****   Age:  35  Education:  High School diploma  Employment:  Works at ****** *******  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Support systems:  Mom reports that they have a lot of family support.  Her sister has been here with her, but is flying back today to ******.  The maternal grandparents reside locally.  *******, ****** states that her mother is 'overbearing' and she prefers that she not be here unless ****** is here.  The paternal grandparents also reside locally and are supportive and helpful.         ****** denies that transportation is a problem.  She states she just bought a new car as her former car was old and not reliable for making the trip back and forth so frequently.  She states the new car is better on gas as well.  She can make the trip here and home 2 ½ times on a tank of gas.  However, as she is currently not working, she admits that the cost of gas is becoming overwhelming.  ****** states that they are interested in fundraising.  They were given information on ****.  They are also interested in applying for a First Hand Foundation *****.  The application was provided to them.       ******* is the first child for this family.  ****** disclosed that they were unaware of his heart defect until after he was born.  She disclosed that they were preparing themselves for the worst outcomes but hoping for the best.  She states that having some background in the medical field has helped prepare her a little.  While working at ******* transport, she has been exposed to medically fragile patients ranging from dialysis patients to hospital discharges to hospice. She disclosed she has had some hospice patients pass away during transport.  In light of this, she believes she will have no difficulty administering meds, feeds, etc.  She plans to be the primary caregiver post-transplant.  ****** will be present at the time of transplant but has a limited amount of paid time off available.       Course of illness:     ******* was born by C section at 36 weeks of gestation for premature rupture of membranes, pre-eclampsia, and hypertension.  He experienced respiratory distress in the delivery room and was transferred to the NICU.   He decompensated on day 3 of life and was emergently intubated.  He was diagnosed with Hypoplastic left heart syndrome.  He was then transferred to the ***** for further care.  After cardiac cath and MRI, it was decided to move forward with surgical intervention while also evaluating for heart transplant          Financial Situation:     ******* is covered by Medicaid ********.  The family has already applied him for SSI/ disability.  However, he has not yet been approved.  Currently the family is supported by dad's income.  ****** states her employer is holding a job for her but understands her current situation.  She is not on FMLA but is not in danger of losing her job.  She plans to return to work eventually.  Her leave is not paid leave.  The family does verbalize willingness to *********.  She is also applying for WIC.       Family History:     There is a history of hypertension on the maternal side of the family.  In addition, the maternal grandmother has a history of cancer and of A Fib.  The paternal grandparents both have a history of cancer.  ****** states that both she and ****** are healthy.  She did have hypertension in her pregnancy however.        There is no reported mental health history, other than ****** having an episode of depression about 10 years ago when she and her fiancé at the time broke up.  She also admits to some anxiety in relation to *******'s hospitalization.  ****** was tearful and somewhat anxious during this evaluation, secondary to ******* having just been intubated.         The family denies any substance abuse in the immediate family.  However, she states that she formerly smoked.  She states she quit smoking when she ******* she was pregnant.  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF.       Adherence:  There are no concerns related to adherence that have been identified.  The family denies that there will be any difficulty keeping follow up appointments, obtaining labs, etc.  ****** states that they are only about a 30 minute drive from the hospital.  She is making this trip almost daily, and states it will not be a problem to keep weekly appointments.  She states she feels comfortable being able to administer medications. She is aware that ******* could possible have feeding issues as he has never been fed by mouth. She verbalizes belief that g-tube feeds would be manageable for her to do as well, if needed.     Assessment and recommendations:     ****** states that she and ****** have been in a whirlwind since *******'s birth, as they were not expecting him to be medically fragile.  She states they are hopeful he will be ok, but are aware that there are possibilities of complications. She states she has not yet heard the most recent MRI results and is hopeful that he is ok neurologically.  She states she understands why ******* was intubated today and is hopeful he will do fine in the surgery next week.  She states that she and ****** both desire to do whatever it takes for *******, and are open to moving forward with transplant. She would be interested in speaking to another mother of a heart transplant baby.          IMPRESSION:  (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  11  Low/Moderate     The family scores as low to moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concerns are the financial stressors.  It is expected that this can be successfully managed. Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.   *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission         ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
